| `preview` | A built-in preview drawn on the block. `embed` draws the block's embed as Discord shows it, `canvas` its picture (both make the block wider). |

### requires

| Key | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `intents` | Discord gateway intents the block needs, such as `GuildMessages` or `GuildMembers`. The bot asks Discord for the intents of the blocks used. |
| `dependencies` | npm packages the block's code needs: `{ "node-fetch": "^3.3.0" }`. They're installed before Run and listed in exports. Load them with [`ctx.require`](./ctx#require). |
| `assets` | Files the block needs in the bot, such as fonts or pictures, as paths relative to the block file: `["../../fonts/MyFont.ttf"]`. They go into the bot (and into exports) with the block; [`ctx.asset(name)`](./ctx#asset) gives a path to one. Only files inside the plugin's own folder: one from elsewhere is left out, with a line in Problems. |
| `permissions` | The bot's permissions the block needs, by the platform's flag names: `["ManageRoles"]`, or a list per value of one field: `{ action: { kick: ["KickMembers"], ban: ["BanMembers"] } }`. When the platform answers "Missing Permissions", the error names them. |

Discord's privileged intents (`GuildMembers`, `GuildPresences`, `MessageContent`) have to be turned on for the bot in the developer portal; Bot settings lists the ones the project's blocks need, with a link there.

## run

```js
async run({ fields, ctx, node }) { … }
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `fields` | Every field's value, with `${…}` already filled in and connected values read. |
| `ctx` | The [run context](./ctx): logging, variables, stored data, the Discord client… |
| `node` | `{ id, workspace }`: which block on which canvas is running. |

What `run` does depends on the kind:

- **Value blocks** return their outputs: `return { result: 42 }`. They run when an action needs one of the outputs.
- **Actions without `flows`** return their outputs (or nothing). The flow continues on their single action output after `run` finishes.
- **Actions with `flows`** call [`ctx.next(flow, outputs)`](./ctx#next) for the way to continue, once or several times (a loop calls it for every item).

`run` may be `async`; write it that way only when it awaits something. The block picker tags a block **Async** when its `run` waits for something (Discord, the web, a timer, stored data): when it uses `await`, `.then(` or a new `Promise`. Waiting for the rest of the flow (`await ctx.next(…)`) doesn't count. Every other action and value block is **Sync**. Searching for *async* or *sync* finds them.

Throw an `Error` to fail the block; the message is shown on the block and in the Console.

## flows

```js
flows: ["true", "false"],
async run({ fields, ctx }) {
  await ctx.next(fields.condition ? "true" : "false");
}
```

Each name becomes an action output. A loop:

```js
flows: ["each", "done"],
outputs: { item: { type: "any" }, index: { type: "number" } },
async run({ fields, ctx }) {
  for (const [index, item] of fields.list.entries()) await ctx.next("each", { item, index });
  await ctx.next("done");
}
```

## listen

Event blocks subscribe in `listen(ctx, emit)`. Each call of `emit(outputs)` starts a new run with those outputs; it returns a promise of the value the run gives back with Return.

```js
listen(ctx, emit) {
  ctx.discord.client.on("guildMemberAdd", (member) => {
    emit({ member, user: member.user, server: member.guild });
  });
},
```

`ctx.fields` holds the event block's own field values. Use [`ctx.runtime.onStart`](./ctx#runtime) for work that should wait until the bot is connected.

## define

`define()` runs **in the editor** (in a sandbox, with a 50 ms limit) whenever the block's values or connections change. It changes the block's shape: extra fields, hidden fields, the type of an output. It can't do anything else: no network, no files.

```js
define({ values, connected, project }) {
  // A For Each over a list of members gives members.
  return { outputs: { item: { type: circuit.types.elementOf(connected.list) } } };
}
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `values` | The values filled in on the block. |
| `connected` | The type string of what's connected to each input, by field key. |
| `project` | `{ data, settings }`: the project's data, such as `slashCommands`, and Bot › Settings (without secrets), such as `databases`. |

It returns a [DefineResult](./fields#define-results): `add`, `hide`, `set`, `outputs`, `flows`. The global `circuit` has helpers: `circuit.types.elementOf("list<discord.role>")` is `"discord.role"`, `circuit.types.shape("object<{ name: text }>")` is `{ name: "text" }`, and `circuit.object.keysToChoices(shape)` turns a shape into choices.

Top-level `require()` calls return a harmless stand-in in the editor, so a block file that needs a package at run time still loads.

## migrate

```js
info: { …, version: "2.0.0" },
migrate(values, fromVersion) {
  // In version 1, "message" was called "text".
  if (fromVersion === "1") return { ...values, message: values.text };
  return values;
}
```

When a project saved with an older **major** version opens, XC Circuit calls `migrate` with the saved values and the old major version, saves what it returns, and updates the block to the new version. Without `migrate`, the values are kept as they are.

## TypeScript

Block files can be `.ts`. For types in your code editor, use the `@xc-circuit/sdk` package (in the repository's [`sdk/`](https://github.com/XCraftTM/XC-Circuit/tree/main/sdk) folder):

```ts
import { defineBlock } from "@xc-circuit/sdk";

interface Fields { xp: number; perLevel: number }

export default defineBlock<Fields>({
  id: "demo.level_from_xp",
  kind: "value",
  info: { name: "Level From XP", description: "Turns XP into a level.", author: "You", version: "1.0.0" },
  fields: { xp: { type: "number", pin: true }, perLevel: { type: "number", default: 100 } },
  outputs: { level: { type: "number" } },
  run({ fields }) {
    return { level: Math.floor(fields.xp / fields.perLevel) + 1 };
  },
});
```

`defineBlock` only helps the types: it returns the block unchanged.

## Writing good blocks

- **English, plain words.** Names in Title Case, descriptions for people who don't program.
- **One job per block.** Combine blocks on the canvas rather than adding modes to one.
- **Accept ids and objects.** Where a block needs a user, take a user, a member or an id.
- **Fail with a reason.** `throw new Error("Connect a channel or type its id")`, not a stack trace.
- **Keep ids and field keys stable.** Projects store them.


---

<!-- docs/api/fields.md · https://xcrafttm.github.io/XC-Circuit/api/fields -->

# Fields and types

::: info In short
A block's `fields` are what people fill in on it (or connect a wire to); each has a `type` that decides its editor and which wires fit.
:::

## Field options

```js
fields: {
  mode: { type: "select", default: "reply", pin: false, choices: { reply: "Reply", send: "Send to channel" } },
  channel: { type: "discord.channel", pin: "only", show: { mode: ["send"] }, description: "Where to send it." },
  text: { type: "textarea", default: "", description: "The message. ${…} holds JavaScript." },
  delay: { type: "number", default: 0, min: 0, step: 0.5, advanced: true, label: "Delay (s)" },
}
```

| Key | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | text | **Required.** A [type string](#type-strings) or one of the [editors](#field-editors) below. |
| `label` | text | The name shown. Default: the key, in words (`deleteAfter` → *Delete after*). |
| `description` | text | Help shown on hover and in the Inspector. |
| `default` | any | The value of a new block. |
| `required` | boolean | Empty is a problem (listed in Problems). |
| `pin` | `"auto"` · `true` · `false` · `"only"` | `"auto"` (default): filled in on the block, with a pin toggle. `true`: starts as a pin. `false`: never a pin. `"only"`: must be connected (inputs whose pin type has [`fromId`](./pin-types#finding-values-by-id), such as channels, can still be switched to a box for an id). |
| `multi` | boolean | The pin accepts several wires; the block gets their values as one list. |
| `advanced` | boolean | An option used less often. On the block it goes below **More options**, folded to start with: folded, it shows only when it's in use (a pin, connected, or set to something other than its default). The Inspector lists it under *More options*; its **pin** chip (also for `pin: "only"` fields) puts its pin on the block. |
| `show` | object | Shown only when other fields have one of these values: `{ mode: ["send", "edit"] }`. |
| `choices` | object | For `select`: value → label. A nested object makes a group: `{ "Text": { plain: "Plain", bold: "Bold" } }`. |
| `template` | boolean | Whether `${…}` in the text is filled in. Default: yes for text fields and colours. |
| `templateParts` | boolean | Instead of filling `${…}` in, give the block `{ strings, values }`: the text around them and their values, as a JavaScript tagged template gets them. SQL Query uses it to send the values as parameters. |
| `min`, `max`, `step` | number | For numbers. |
| `placeholder` | text | Grey hint in an empty text box. |
| `custom` | boolean | For a field with `choices`: the list ends in **Custom…**, which shows a text box for any other value (and so does a value that isn't one of the choices). The value stays one text, so a `text` field like this can still be connected. Get Property uses it for the properties of the connected value. |
| `suggest` | `"button"`, `"select"` or `"form"`: a custom id field of an event. It offers the ids of that kind the project gives (in layouts, forms and fields with `customIdOf`), with Custom… for others, and Problems checks the two match. |
| `customIdOf` | `"button"`, `"select"` or `"form"`: this field gives a button, menu or form its custom id (Button, Select Menu). |
| `pick` | `"channel"`, `"voice"`, `"category"` or `"role"`: a text field for an id (or name) that gets a button listing the bot's servers' channels or roles; picking one puts its id in. Fields for channels by id get it from their type. |

## Field editors

Besides the [type strings](#type-strings), a field's `type` can name an editor:

| Type | Editor | Value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | a text box | text |
| `textarea` | a box of several lines, resizable | text |
| `number` | number box | number |
| `boolean` | switch | `true` / `false` |
| `select` | drop-down of `choices` | the chosen value |
| `multiselect` | drop-down of `choices` with a checkbox each (and a search when there are many) | a list of the chosen keys; text with commas from older projects is read too |
| `color` | swatch with a colour picker, or (with its `${}` button) `${…}` text for a colour from the bot; like other fields it can also be a pin | `"#RRGGBB"`; from a pin or `${…}`, any hex colour with or without `#` (`#FF5CA8`, `FF5CA8`, `#F5A`), which the block reads as a colour |
| `embed` | the Embed Builder (Discord) | embed object |
| `layout` | the Layout Builder, and the message on the block (Discord) | Components V2: `{ components: [ … ] }` |
| `modal` | the Modal Builder, and the form on the block (Discord) | Discord's modal JSON: `{ title, custom_id, components: [ … ] }`, with questions (type 18 around a text input, select menu or file upload) and texts (type 10) |
| `slash-command-ref` | a slash command of the project (Discord) | its name |
| `canvas` | the Canvas Builder, and the picture on the block | a design: `{ width, height, background, layers, samples }` ([Build Canvas](/explanations/canvas)) |

## Type strings

Types say what a pin carries. The editor only connects pins whose types fit.

| Type | Values |
| --- | --- |
| `text`, `number`, `boolean`, `date` | the basic values |
| `object` | any object |
| `any` | anything; fits everywhere |
| `list<T>` | a list of `T`: `list<text>`, `list<discord.member>` |
| `T?` | a `T` or nothing: `discord.member?` |
| `A \| B` | either |
| `object<{ name: text, xp: number }>` | an object with these keys |
| `discord.user`, `fluxer.message`, … | [pin types](./pin-types) from plugins |

A type fits where its parent type is expected (`discord.member` extends `object`), and plugins can declare [conversions](./pin-types#conversions) (a member fits where a user is needed).

## define results

[`define()`](./blocks#define) returns any of these:

| Key | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `add` | More fields, by key, as field options. They go after the block's own fields, unless a field says `after`: the key of the field it follows, or `""` for the very top (Send Message puts what it sends to there). |
| `hide` | Keys of fields to hide. |
| `set` | Changes to existing fields: `{ text: { label: "Reason", required: true } }`. |
| `outputs` | Outputs to add or replace, by key: `{ item: { type: "discord.role" } }`. |
| `flows` | Replaces the block's `flows`. |

Example: Slash Command adds an output for each option of the chosen command.

```js
define({ values, project }) {
  const cmd = (project.data?.slashCommands || []).find((c) => c.name === values.command);
  const outputs = {};
  for (const o of cmd?.options || []) outputs[o.name] = { type: "text", description: o.description };
  return { outputs };
}
```


---

<!-- docs/api/ctx.md · https://xcrafttm.github.io/XC-Circuit/api/ctx -->

# Run context (ctx)

::: info In short
Inside a block's `run()`, `ctx` is the running bot: `ctx.next()` to continue a flow, `ctx.log`, variables (`ctx.vars`), saved data (`ctx.store`), the Discord client (`ctx.discord.client`) and more.
:::

Blocks get `ctx` in [`run({ fields, ctx, node })`](./blocks#run), [`listen(ctx, emit)`](./blocks#listen) and `setup(ctx)`. It's how a block reaches the running bot: logging, variables, stored data, signals, and the libraries of the build mode.

This runs in the **bot** (Node.js), not in the editor.

## next

```js
await ctx.next(flow, outputs?)
```

Continues the flow on one of the block's [`flows`](./blocks#flows), after setting `outputs`. Resolves when everything after it has finished, so a loop can call it once per item. Only actions with `flows` call it.

## wired

```js
ctx.wired(flow) // true or false
```

Whether this block's `flow` output has a wire. For a path that handles a case some projects don't care about, such as Find Role's **Missing**: take it when it's connected, and fail as before when it isn't. Apps older than 0.1.9 don't have it, so check with `ctx.wired?.("missing")`.

## set

```js
ctx.set("progress", 50)
```

Sets one output without continuing. Useful in loops, or before a `next` that doesn't pass outputs.

## id

`"workspace:node"`: this block in this workspace, for keeping data of its own (in [`ctx.store.ns`](#store), say), apart from other copies of the block.

## fields

The block's own field values as filled in (without connected values). In `run`, prefer the `fields` argument, which includes connected values.

## typed · authored

`ctx.typed(key)` is what the bot's author typed into field `key`, before `${…}` was filled in, and `undefined` when the field is connected. `ctx.authored(key)` says whether the field is exactly that: not connected and without `${…}`.

A value that isn't authored may come from what the bot's users type (a command option, a message). Treat it so where that matters: a web address only to the public web, a file only inside the bot's files folder.

```js
const publicOnly = !ctx.authored("url") && !fields.privateOk;
const { res, body } = await ctx.util.fetch(fields.url, {}, { publicOnly, maxBytes: 10 * 1024 * 1024 });
```

## event

The outputs of the event that started this run: `ctx.event.user`, `ctx.event.message`… Undefined in `listen` and `setup`.

## log

```js
ctx.log.info("Synced", count, "roles");
ctx.log.success("Done");
ctx.log.warn("Slow answer");
ctx.log.error("Could not reach the API");
ctx.log.debug({ payload });
```

Writes to the Console (and, in exported bots, the terminal), naming the block. Objects are shown readably.

## vars

Variables in memory, gone when the bot stops. See [Variables and stored data](/explanations/data).

```js
ctx.vars.run.set("total", 3);           // this run only
ctx.vars.workspace.get("queue", []);    // shared by this workspace's runs
ctx.vars.global.has("ready");           // shared by the whole bot
```

Each has `get(name, fallback?)`, `set(name, value)`, `has(name)` and `delete(name)`.

## store

Data kept in `store.json`, which survives restarts.

```js
const xp = await ctx.store.member(server.id, user.id).inc("xp", 5);
await ctx.store.global().set("lastRestart", Date.now());
```

| Scope | Values per |
| --- | --- |
| `ctx.store.global()` | bot |
| `ctx.store.server(id)` | server |
| `ctx.store.user(id)` | user |
| `ctx.store.member(serverId, userId)` | member of a server |
| `ctx.store.channel(id)` | channel |
| `ctx.store.ns(name)` | your own namespace: keep a plugin's data apart |

Each scope has (all return promises):

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `get(key, fallback?)` | The value, or `fallback`. |
| `set(key, value)` | Stores a value (anything JSON can hold). |
| `has(key)` | Whether there's a value. |
| `delete(key)` | Removes it. |
| `inc(key, by = 1)` | Adds to a number (from 0) and gives the new number. |
| `push(key, value)` | Appends to a list (from empty) and gives the list. |
| `keys()` | Every key in this scope. |

`ctx.store.each(scope, serverId?)` lists every stored entity of a scope: `[{ id, values }]`, for leaderboards. Writes are saved to disk within a quarter of a second.

## signal

```js
ctx.signal.emit("level-up", { user, level });
```

Starts every **On Signal** event with that name, without waiting for them.

## runtime

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `onStart(fn)` | Runs `fn` once the bot has started and is connected. |
| `onSignal(name, fn)` | Runs `fn(data)` for each signal with that name. |
| `onError(fn)` | Runs `fn(error)` for errors outside any Try Zone. |
| `onCall(name, fn)` | Answers Call blocks with that name: `fn(data)` starts a run and resolves to what it returns. |
| `call(name, data)` | Runs the When Called flows with that name and resolves to the first one's return value. |
| `setting(name)` | A setting of Bot › Settings (not a secret). |
| `dataDir` | The bot's data folder (stored data, SQLite files, the files folder `files/`). |
| `secret(name)` | A secret of Bot › Settings, such as an API key a [plugin's page](./build-modes#plugin-settings) asks for. |

## returnValue

```js
ctx.returnValue(value)
```

Sets what this run gives back to the Call block (or `emit`) that started it. The Return block uses this.

## resolve

```js
const fresh = await ctx.resolve();
```

Reads the block's inputs again. Loops whose condition changes while they run (Loop While) use it.

## project

`{ name, mode, settings, data }`: the project's name, build mode, settings (without secrets) and data, such as `data.slashCommands`. `settings.databases` lists the databases (without passwords).

## fill

```js
ctx.fill("Hello ${name}!", { name: "Alex" })
```

Fills `${…}` in a text the way text fields are filled: from the event, run variables, earlier outputs and the names you pass.

## db

```js
const db = ctx.db("default");              // or a database's name, or its id
const rows = await db.select("levels", [{ column: "xp", op: ">", value: 100 }], { order: "xp", desc: true, limit: 10 });
const { id } = await db.insert("levels", { user_id: user.id, xp: 0 });
await db.update("levels", { xp: 50 }, [{ column: "user_id", op: "=", value: user.id }]);
await db.remove("levels", [{ column: "user_id", op: "=", value: user.id }]);
const { rows: top } = await db.run("SELECT * FROM levels WHERE xp > ?", [100]);
```

A database of [Bot › Settings › Databases](/explanations/databases). `"default"` (or nothing) is the default one. It connects the first time it's used; every block shares the connection.

`ctx.db({ kind, host, port, user, password, database, ssl, url })` connects to a database the block is given instead (`kind` is `"mariadb"`, `"postgres"` or `"mongodb"`; `url` instead of the others). It throws unless Bot › Settings › Databases allows [databases given on blocks](/explanations/databases#a-database-given-on-the-block). The same details give the same connection; up to 8 stay open. List the kind's npm package in your block's `requires.dependencies`, since the bundle only adds drivers for the databases of Bot › Settings and the built-in blocks.

| Method | Gives |
| --- | --- |
| `select(table, conditions?, { order, desc, limit, offset, any }?)` | The rows, as objects. |
| `insert(table, values)` | `{ id, row }`: the new row's id, and the row where the database gives it back. |
| `update(table, values, conditions?, any?)` | How many rows changed. |
| `remove(table, conditions?, any?)` | How many rows were deleted. |
| `query(sql)` | `{ rows, affected, id }`. `sql` is text, or `{ strings, values }` from a [`templateParts`](./fields#field-options) field: the values are sent as parameters. Not for MongoDB. |
| `run(sql, params)` | The same, with your own parameters: `?` for MariaDB, MySQL and SQLite, `$1, $2…` for PostgreSQL. |
| `describe()` | `{ version, tables }`. |

A condition is `{ column, op, value }`; `op` is `"="`, `"!="`, `">"`, `">="`, `"<"`, `"<="`, `"contains"`, `"starts"`, `"ends"` (these three ignore upper and lower case), `"null"` or `"notNull"`. With `any`, one condition is enough. Table and column names must be letters, digits and `_` (a `.` between schema and table); values are always sent as parameters. `db.kind` is `"mariadb"`, `"postgres"`, `"sqlite"` or `"mongodb"`, and `db.client` the driver's own pool or client once connected.

## timers

```js
const { id, due } = await ctx.timers.schedule({ name: "reminder", due: Date.now() + 600000, data: { text }, key: `remind-${user.id}` });
await ctx.timers.cancel({ key: `remind-${user.id}` });   // or { id } or { name }; gives how many
const waiting = await ctx.timers.list("reminder");       // soonest first
ctx.timers.on("reminder", (t) => { /* t.data, t.due, t.late */ }, { catchUp: true });
```

One-time timers, kept with the [stored data](#store) so they survive restarts. `on` is for event blocks' `listen`; missed timers (more than a minute late) reach only listeners with `catchUp`. `data` is kept as JSON: live objects become their data.

## asset

```js
const font = ctx.asset("../../fonts/MyFont.ttf");
```

The path on disk of a file the block lists in [`requires.assets`](./blocks#requires), as written there. It's written into the bot's data folder the first time.

## util

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `sleep(ms)` | A promise that resolves after `ms` milliseconds. |
| `isURL(text)` | Whether the text is a web address. |
| `id(length = 10)` | A random id of letters and digits. |
| `shuffle(list)` | A shuffled copy. |
| `typeOf(value)` | `"null"`, `"list"`, or JavaScript's `typeof`. |
| `fetch(url, init?, { publicOnly, maxBytes, redirects }?)` | `fetch`, guarded: resolves to `{ res, body }` with the body as a Buffer, read up to `maxBytes` (10 MB; more fails). With `publicOnly`, the address and each redirect must be on the public web, not this computer, a private network or a cloud's metadata service. |
| `checkPublic(url)` | Throws unless a web address is public, as above. |

## bot

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `uptime` | Milliseconds since the bot started. |
| `stop()` | Stops the bot. |
| `restart()` | Restarts the bot. |

## abortSignal

Inside a [Try Zone](/explanations/errors) with a timeout: an `AbortSignal` that fires when the zone gives up. Pass it to `fetch` and other APIs that accept one, so long work stops in time.

## require

```js
const fetch = ctx.require("node-fetch");
```

Loads an npm package. List it in the block's [`requires.dependencies`](./blocks#requires) so it's installed before Run and included in exports. Node's own modules (`node:crypto`, `node:fs`) work too.

## Mode libraries

[Runtime libraries](./runtime-libs) add their API under their id:

| Mode | Member | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Discord Bot | `ctx.discord.client` | the discord.js `Client` |
| Fluxer Bot | `ctx.fluxer.client`, `ctx.fluxer.prefix()`, `ctx.fluxer.channel(v)`, `ctx.fluxer.user(v)`, `ctx.fluxer.member(v, server)`… | the fluxer.js client and helpers that accept objects or ids |


---

<!-- docs/api/editor.md · https://xcrafttm.github.io/XC-Circuit/api/editor -->

# Editor plugins (xc)

::: info In short
An `editor.js` in your plugin, named in `plugin.toml` under `[editor] script = "editor.js"`. It uses the global `xc` to add commands, panels, checks and overlays to XC™ Circuit, and to read and change the project. It reloads when you save it.
:::

```js
xc.command({ id: "hello.greet", title: "Say hello", run() { xc.log("Hello from", xc.project()?.name) } });
```

Types for your code editor: `/// <reference types="@xc-circuit/sdk/editor" />` (from the repository's `sdk/` folder).

## Quick reference

### Add things to the app

| | |
| --- | --- |
| [`xc.command({ id, title, run })`](#xc-command) | a command in the Plugins menu and the command palette |
| [`xc.panel({ id, title, render })`](#xc-panel) | a dockable panel |
| [`xc.check(fn)`](#xc-check) | problems for the Problems panel |
| [`xc.overlay({ id, width, height, render, onClick })`](#xc-overlay) | something floating over the editor |
| [`xc.on(event, fn)`](#xc-on) | react to `"save"`, `"botEvent"`, `"selection"` |
| [`xc.every(ms, fn)` · `xc.after(ms, fn)` · `xc.cancel(id)`](#timers) | timers |
| [`xc.playSound(file, { volume })`](#sounds) | play a sound from the plugin |
| [`xc.tool({ name, description, input, run })`](#xc-tool) | something AI agents can do through the MCP server |

### Read the project

| | |
| --- | --- |
| `xc.project()` | `{ name, root }` or `null` |
| `xc.workspaces()` | `[{ key, name }]` |
| `xc.workspace(key)` | a workspace as saved: `{ name, nodes, links, zones, notes }` |
| `xc.blocks()` | every block: `[{ workspace, id, type, values, … }]` |
| `xc.activeWorkspace()` · `xc.selection()` | what's open and selected |
| `xc.blockName(type)` | `"core.log"` → `"Log"` |
| `xc.data.get(key)` | project data (the project's `data`) |
| `xc.storage.get(key)` | the plugin's own store (on this computer) |
| `xc.botRunning()` · `xc.screen()` | is the bot running · window size |
| `xc.blockTypes(query)` · `xc.blockType(type)` | installed block types · one type's fields, outputs and flows |
| `xc.blockSource(type)` · `xc.plugins()` | a block type's code: `{ type, plugin, file, version, source }` · the plugins, turned on or off, with their blocks |
| `xc.appSettings()` · `xc.botSettings()` | the app's settings (with the shortcuts) · Bot › Settings: `{ mode, pages, settings: [{ key, label, type, page, value, … }] }` (secrets only say whether one is saved) |
| `xc.server()` | the bot's server (Bot › Remote…): kind, where, `runTarget` (`local` or `server`), `canRunThere`, `savedHere` (false for a server that came with the project's files and the user hasn't saved on this computer: nothing is sent to it), `state`, CPU and memory, `lastUpload`, the server console's last lines; never a password or key |
| `xc.blockPins(workspace, id)` | a block as it is now: its values and pins, with types and wires |
| `xc.problems()` · `xc.console(lines)` | what the Problems panel and the Console show |
| `xc.t(text)` | text in the app's language, from the plugins' `locales/*.toml` |

### Change things

| | |
| --- | --- |
| `xc.addBlock(workspace, type, { x, y, values })` | place a block, returns its id |
| `xc.setWorkspace(key, workspace)` | replace a workspace |
| `xc.connect(workspace, "3.next", "4.in")` | draw a wire, checked like one drawn on the canvas |
| `xc.addWorkspace(name, { folder })` | make a workspace, returns its key |
| `xc.copyText(text)` | put text on the clipboard |
| `xc.fieldValue(type, field, value)` | a value as the block keeps it: embeds, layouts and canvases as the builders save them |
| `xc.openBuilder(workspace, id, field)` | open the Embed, Layout or Canvas Builder on a block's field |
| `xc.blockRects(workspace)` | where its blocks are and how big, as drawn: `{ id: [x, y, width, height] }` |
| `xc.select(workspace, ids)` · `xc.reveal(workspace, id, zoom?)` | select · go to a block (at `zoom` percent, 25 to 200, when given) |
| `xc.data.set(key, value)` · `xc.storage.set(key, value)` | save data (not the key `hosting`: the bot's server is the user's to set, in Bot › Remote…) |
| `xc.log(…)` · `xc.success(…)` · `xc.warn(…)` · `xc.error(…)` | write to the Console |
| `xc.setBotSettings({ key: value })` | change Bot › Settings (not secrets), checked against each setting's type and choices; returns the keys changed |
| `xc.run(id)` | run a command: a plugin's, or `"bot.run"`, `"bot.stop"`, `"file.save"`, `"server.upload"`, `"server.start"`, `"server.restart"`, `"server.stop"`, `"server.kill"`, `"run.local"`, `"run.server"`. Starting the bot or acting on its server (`bot.run`, `server.*`, `run.*`) only works from a command or a click (a button, a link, an overlay's `onClick`) or an agent's tool, not from a timer, a check or `render`: it throws there |
| `xc.moveOverlay(id, x, y)` · `xc.overlayPosition(id)` | move an overlay |

Every change can be undone with Ctrl+Z, like your own edits.

## Adding things

### xc.command

```js
xc.command({ id: "acme.tidy", title: "Tidy up", description: "Shown on hover", run() { … } });
```

The `id` must be unique: start it with your plugin's id.

### xc.panel

```js
xc.panel({ id: "stats", title: "Stats", render(ui) { ui.heading("Hello") } });
```

Opened from the Plugins menu. `render(ui)` describes the panel with [`ui`](./panels); it runs whenever the panel is drawn, so it always shows the current project.

### xc.check

```js
xc.check(() =>
  xc.blocks()
    .filter((b) => b.type === "core.log" && !b.values.message)
    .map((b) => ({ message: "Log has no message", workspace: b.workspace, block: b.id })),
);
```

Runs about once a second. Return problems: a text, or `{ message, workspace, block }` (then clicking the problem selects the block).

### xc.overlay

```js
xc.overlay({
  id: "pet",
  width: 96, height: 96,
  x: -28, y: -60,            // where it starts; negative: from the right or bottom edge
  render(ui) { ui.image("art/pet.svg", { width: 96 }) },
  onClick() { xc.playSound("sounds/boop.wav") },
});
```

Floats over the whole editor. People can drag it (`draggable: false` stops that). `frame: true` puts it on a card. Drawn again after a click, a timer or an event, and at least once a second. Example: [Desk Pet](https://github.com/XCraftTM/XC-Circuit/tree/main/examples/plugins/desk-pet).

### xc.on

| Event | When | `fn` gets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `"save"` | the project was saved | — |
| `"selection"` | other blocks were selected | `{ workspace, blocks }` |
| `"botEvent"` | the bot (run from the editor) did something | `{ type: "started" }`, `{ type: "stopped" }`, `{ type: "log", level, text }`, `{ type: "block", workspace, block, phase, ms, error }` |

Block events come for every block that runs: keep that handler quick.

### Timers

```js
const id = xc.every(500, () => { … });   // every half second (at least 50 ms)
xc.after(2000, () => xc.cancel(id));      // once, two seconds later
```

They also work at the top of the script. A timer that throws is stopped and the error logged.

### Sounds

```js
xc.playSound("sounds/ding.wav", { volume: 0.5 });
```

WAV, MP3 or Ogg Vorbis from the plugin's folder. Nothing plays (and nothing fails) without an audio device.

### xc.tool

Something AI agents such as Claude can do in XC Circuit, through its [MCP server](/explanations/ai-agents). `input` is a JSON Schema for the arguments; `run(args)` returns the answer: text, or any value (the agent gets it as JSON). Throwing an error tells the agent what went wrong. A tool may take 5 seconds.

```js
xc.tool({
  name: "count_blocks",
  description: "How many blocks each workspace has.",
  input: { type: "object", properties: {} },
  run() {
    return xc.workspaces().map((w) => ({ workspace: w.name, blocks: Object.keys(xc.workspace(w.key).nodes).length }));
  },
});
```

The tools of every plugin that is on are offered together; the bundled AI agents plugin has the usual ones. `xc.agents` (`clients()`, `install(id)`, `remove(id)`, `snippet()`, `link()`) is what its panel uses to add the server to AI clients.

## Good to know

**Sandbox.** Scripts run in their own JavaScript engine (QuickJS) and only reach the app through `xc`: no files, no network, no programs. That's why they load without asking you first.

**Time limits.** A render, check or event may take 100 ms; a command, click or save 1 s. Longer, and it's stopped with an error. Memory: 32 MB per plugin.

**Errors** name the file and line: in the Console for commands and events, in the Problems panel for checks, in the panel itself for panels.

**Modules.** `require("./lib/util.js")` loads another file of the plugin (`.js`, `.ts`, `.json`). Only the plugin's own files: not one a link in its folder points to elsewhere, and no name with a colon in it.

**State.** Variables at the top of the script live until the script reloads. Use `xc.storage` for what should last, `xc.data` for what belongs to the project. Keys in `xc.data` are shared, so prefix yours: `"acme.notes"`.

**Not while loading.** The top of the script registers things (and may start timers). The project is only reachable inside the functions you register.

Bigger example: DemoBot's `plugins/demo.custom/editor.js` (panel, command, check).


---

<!-- docs/api/panels.md · https://xcrafttm.github.io/XC-Circuit/api/panels -->

# Panels (ui)

::: info In short
`render(ui)` of a [panel](./editor#xc-panel) or [overlay](./editor#xc-overlay) lists what to show, top to bottom: `ui.heading("…")`, `ui.button("…", onClick)`… XC Circuit draws it with the same UI kit as the rest of the app (its buttons, switches, dropdowns, numbers and colours, in the theme in use) and calls `render` again when something changes.
:::

A panel's `render(ui)` describes what it shows by calling `ui` methods in order. XC Circuit draws the result with the app's own look and theme.

```js
xc.panel({
  id: "stats",
  title: "Stats",
  render(ui) {
    ui.heading("Project");
    ui.row((ui) => {
      ui.stat("workspaces", xc.workspaces().length);
      ui.stat("blocks", xc.blocks().length);
    });
    ui.section("Actions", (ui) => {
      ui.button("Save", () => xc.run("file.save"), { primary: true });
    });
  },
});
```

## How panels update

- `render` runs when the panel is drawn: when it's opened, after a click or a change in it, and at most four times a second otherwise (about once a second while nothing else happens).
- Handlers (the functions given to buttons, links, check boxes and inputs) run when the person uses that element; the panel is drawn again right after.
- Panels are **controlled**: an input shows the value `render` gives it. Store what the person types (in a variable, `xc.storage` or `xc.data`) and give it back on the next render, or it will be undone.

## Elements

Every method returns `ui`, so calls can be chained.

### Text

| Method | Shows |
| --- | --- |
| `ui.heading(text)` | A bold title. |
| `ui.text(text, options?)` | A paragraph; wraps. |
| `ui.muted(text)` | Grey text, for hints. |
| `ui.stat(label, value)` | A big value with a small label under it. Put several in a `row`. |

`ui.text` options:

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `muted` | grey |
| `bold` | strong |
| `mono` | monospaced |
| `size` | font size in points (default 12.5) |
| `color` | `"accent"`, `"success"`, `"warning"`, `"error"`, `"muted"` or `"#RRGGBB"` |

### Controls

| Method | Shows |
| --- | --- |
| `ui.button(label, onClick, options?)` | A button. Options: `primary` (filled with the accent), `tooltip`. Without `onClick` it's disabled. |
| `ui.link(label, onClick, options?)` | A link-style button. Options: `tooltip`. |
| `ui.checkbox(label, checked, onChange)` | A check box. `onChange(checked)`. |
| `ui.toggle(label, on, onChange)` | A switch, like the app's settings. `onChange(on)`. |
| `ui.select(value, choices, onChange, options?)` | A dropdown. `choices`: `{ value: "Label" }` or `[["value", "Label"], …]` (or plain values). `onChange(value)`. Options: `width` (default 200). |
| `ui.number(value, onChange, options?)` | A number to type or drag. `onChange(number)`. Options: `min`, `max`, `step`, `suffix` (`" px"`). |
| `ui.slider(value, min, max, onChange, options?)` | A slider with its number beside it. `onChange(number)`. Options: `step`, `suffix`. |
| `ui.color(value, onChange)` | A colour with the app's picker. `value` and `onChange(value)` as `"#RRGGBB"`. |
| `ui.note(text, options?)` | A box of text. Options: `tone` (`"info"`, `"warning"` or `"success"`), `title`. |
| `ui.input(value, onChange, options?)` | A text box. `onChange(text)` on every change. Options: `placeholder`, `multiline` (a box of several lines), `key` (keeps the text box's focus when the panel's layout around it changes). |
| `ui.progress(fraction, label?)` | A progress bar, `fraction` from 0 to 1. |
| `ui.image(file, options?)` | A picture from the plugin's folder (PNG, JPEG or SVG). Options: `width`, `height` (default 64), `tint` (a colour, as for text). |

### Layout

| Method | Shows |
| --- | --- |
| `ui.row(fn)` | What `fn(ui)` adds, side by side (wrapping when narrow). |
| `ui.section(title, fn, options?)` | A section with a title that folds open and closed. Options: `open: false` starts it closed. |
| `ui.separator()` | A line. |
| `ui.space(points = 8)` | Empty space. |

`row` and `section` get their own `ui`; use it for what goes inside:

```js
ui.section("Workspaces", (ui) => {
  for (const w of xc.workspaces()) {
    ui.row((ui) => {
      ui.text(w.name, { bold: w.key === xc.activeWorkspace() });
      ui.link("Open", () => xc.reveal(w.key, Object.keys(xc.workspace(w.key).nodes)[0]));
    });
  }
});
```

## Errors

If `render` throws, the panel shows the error with its file and line, above what it showed last. Fix the script and save it: the plugin reloads by itself.


---

<!-- docs/api/plugin-toml.md · https://xcrafttm.github.io/XC-Circuit/api/plugin-toml -->

# plugin.toml

::: info In short
The file that makes a folder a plugin: its `id`, `name` and `version`, and what it adds (`[contributes]`, `[editor]`).
:::

Every plugin folder has a `plugin.toml` at its top. It says what the plugin is and what it contributes.

```toml
id          = "acme.tools"
name        = "Acme Tools"
version     = "1.2.0"
author      = "Acme"
description = "Blocks and a panel for Acme bots."
icon        = "icons/acme.svg"

[engines]
circuit = "^1.0"

[dependencies]
"xc.core" = "^1.0"

[contributes]
blocks  = ["blocks/**/*.{js,ts}"]
themes  = ["themes/*.toml"]
locales = ["locales/*.toml"]

[editor]
script = "editor.js"
```

## Top level

| Key | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | text | **Required.** Unique, lowercase, dotted: `you.plugin`. Block ids usually start with it. |
| `name` | text | **Required.** Shown in the Plugins view and the manager. |
| `version` | text | The plugin's version, `major.minor.patch`. |
| `author` | text | Who made it. |
| `description` | text | One or two sentences, shown under the name. |
| `icon` | path | An SVG or PNG in the plugin folder. |
| `optional` | true / false | For plugins that come with the app: it can be turned off and removed (and added back), unlike the others. |
| `overrides` | list of block ids | Blocks of other plugins this plugin may replace with blocks of the same id. Without it, a second block with an id that exists is refused. |

## `[engines]`

| Key | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `circuit` | The plugin API versions the plugin works with: `"^1.0"`, `"1.x"` or `">=1.0"`. Plugins for another major version aren't loaded. Missing means any. |
| `app` | The oldest XC Circuit version the plugin works with: `"0.2.0"`. Older apps don't load it (and don't download it as a block update). Set it when the plugin's blocks need something only newer apps have. Missing means any. |

When the same plugin (by `id`) is in two folders, the one with the higher `version` loads.

## `[dependencies]`

Other plugins this one needs, by id, with a version range: `"xc.core" = "^1.0"`. They are loaded first; a plugin whose dependencies are missing isn't loaded, and the Problems panel says why.

These are **plugins**. npm packages for the bot go in a block's [`requires.dependencies`](./blocks#requires) or a build mode's [`[dependencies]`](./build-modes#dependencies).

## `[contributes]`

Each entry is a list of paths or glob patterns relative to the plugin folder. `**` matches any folders, `{a,b}` either word. They stay inside the plugin's folder: a pattern that starts at the top of the disk or goes up with `..` is left out, with a line in Problems.

| Key | Contributes | Reference |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `blocks` | block files | [Blocks](./blocks) |
| `buildModes` | build modes | [Build modes](./build-modes) |
| `pinTypes` | pin types | [Pin types](./pin-types) |
| `classes` | class catalogs: the members of the values behind pin types, for completion in `${…}` | [Pin types](./pin-types#class-catalogs) |
| `themes` | themes | [Themes](./themes) |
| `locales` | translations | [Translations](./locales) |
| `botSettings` | pages and settings for Bot › Settings | [Plugin settings](./build-modes#plugin-settings) |
| `icons` | icons, by file name without extension (`icons/rocket.svg` is `rocket`) | — |

Runtime libraries are named by the build mode that uses them ([`runtimeLibs`](./build-modes#keys)), and templates are found in the plugin's `templates/` folder without being listed.

## `[editor]`

| Key | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `script` | The editor script, relative to the plugin folder: `editor.js` or `editor.ts`. Default `editor.js`. See [Editor plugins](./editor). |

A `[native]` section (a compiled Rust library) is no longer loaded: XC Circuit runs editor code written in JavaScript only. Such a plugin's blocks and settings still load, and the Plugins view says its native part isn't supported.

## Where plugins are loaded from

The app's `plugins/` folder, your plugins folder (`%APPDATA%\XC Circuit\plugins` or `~/.local/share/xc-circuit/plugins`), the folders in `XC_CIRCUIT_PLUGINS` (separated like `PATH`), and the open project's `plugins/` folder. Plugin files are watched and reload when saved.


---

<!-- docs/api/build-modes.md · https://xcrafttm.github.io/XC-Circuit/api/build-modes -->

# Build modes

::: info In short
A build mode is a kind of bot (Discord Bot, Fluxer Bot): which blocks it offers, the picker's categories, the settings in Bot › Settings and the npm packages it needs.
:::

A build mode is a kind of bot: *Discord Bot*, *Fluxer Bot*. It decides which blocks the picker offers and how they're sorted, which settings Bot › Settings asks for, which npm packages the bot needs, and which [runtime libraries](./runtime-libs) set the bot up. Modes are TOML files listed in a plugin's `contributes.buildModes`.

```toml
id          = "fluxer-bot"
name        = "Fluxer Bot"
icon        = "message"
description = "A bot for Fluxer, built with fluxer.js."

blocks      = ["xc.core/*", "xc.fluxer/*"]
runtime     = "node"
runtimeLibs = ["xc.fluxer/runtime/fluxer.js"]
exporter    = "xc.fluxer/node-bundle"
tokenEnv    = "FLUXER_BOT_TOKEN"

[[categories]]
id = "send"
name = "Send Messages"
icon = "send"

[[pages]]
id = "connection"
name = "Connection"
icon = "plug"
description = "How your bot logs in to Fluxer."
order = 10

[settings]
token  = { type = "secret", group = "Connection", label = "Bot token", required = true }
prefix = { type = "text", group = "Messages", label = "Text command prefix", default = "!", pattern = '\S{1,5}', patternHint = "1 to 5 characters, without spaces." }

[dependencies]
"@fluxerjs/core" = "^3.3.0"
```

## Keys

| Key | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | **Required.** Unique id, saved in projects' `circuit.project.json` as `mode`. |
| `name` | Shown in File › New Project. |
| `icon` | An icon name. |
| `description` | One sentence, shown in File › New Project. |
| `blocks` | Which blocks appear: `"plugin.id/*"` for all blocks of a plugin. |
| `runtime` | `"node"`. |
| `runtimeLibs` | [Runtime libraries](./runtime-libs), as `"plugin.id/path/in/plugin.js"`: a file inside that plugin's folder. |
| `exporter` | How Bot › Export packages the bot (`"<plugin>/node-bundle"`: a Node.js folder). |
| `tokenEnv` | The environment variable an exported bot reads its token from. Default `DISCORD_TOKEN`. |
| `features` | What the mode's projects have. `"slashCommands"` shows the Slash Command Builder. |
| `privilegedIntents` | A table of intents (as blocks name them) that must be turned on by hand, with what the platform calls each: Bot settings › Privileged intents lists the ones the project's blocks need. |
| `intentsPage` | Where they are turned on; `{appId}` is the bot's application id (from its token). A web address (`https://…`), as `inviteUrl` is: nothing else is opened. |
| `inviteUrl` | A link that adds the bot to a server, offered under the bot token once one is set: `{appId}` is the bot's application id, `{permissions}` the number picked from `invitePermissions`. |
| `invitePermissions` | A table of the permissions to choose from for `inviteUrl`: name (translatable) → the permissions number. The first is picked at first. |

## categories

The block picker's categories, in order. Blocks name one in [`search.category`](./blocks#search).

| Key | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | What blocks refer to. |
| `name` | Shown in the picker (translatable). |
| `icon` | An icon name. |

The Discord mode's categories: `bot`, `commands`, `components`, `send`, `messages`, `design`, `reactions`, `members`, `moderation`, `roles`, `channels`, `server`, `voice`, `premium`, `format`, `flow`, `calls`, `time`, `variables`, `data`, `text`, `numbers`, `lists`, `web`, `code`. Fluxer's are similar, without those Fluxer doesn't have yet (slash commands, components).

## pages

Bot › Settings is a list of pages on the left, like the app's Settings, with the page shown on the right. A mode lists its pages here; [plugins add their own](#plugin-settings).

| Key | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | **Required.** What settings name in `page` (or match with `group`, see below). |
| `name` | Shown in the list and as the page's title (translatable). |
| `icon` | An icon name. |
| `description` | One sentence under the title (translatable). |
| `order` | Where it goes in the list: lower first. Without one it counts as 50; pages with the same order keep the order they're listed in, the mode's first. |

Pages without settings aren't shown. The Discord mode's pages are `connection` (10), `slash-commands` (20), `messages` (30) and `music` (40); Bot › Settings adds **Privileged intents** last for modes that have them.

## settings

The fields of Bot › Settings, by key. Runtime libraries and blocks read them with `rt.setting(key)` / [`ctx.runtime.setting(key)`](./ctx#runtime), and get the `default` until another value is saved.

| Key | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `type` | `"text"` (the default), `"secret"`, `"select"`, `"boolean"`, `"number"`, or one of the [elements](#elements) below. A secret is kept in the credential store, never in the project, and read with `rt.secret(key)`; the key `token` is the bot token. |
| `page` | The `id` of the page it's on. |
| `group` | With `page`: a heading on the page. Without `page`: the page itself, the one whose `id` is the group's name in lower case with dashes (`Slash commands` is `slash-commands`); a page is made for it when there's none. Without both, the setting is on *General*. |
| `label` | Its name. |
| `description` | Help under it. |
| `placeholder` | Grey hint in the empty box. |
| `default` | The value until one is set. |
| `required` | Marked with * in Bot › Settings. |
| `pattern` | A regular expression the value must match; checked as you type. |
| `patternHint` | What to say when it doesn't. |
| `sensitive` | `true` hides a text setting behind the eye button, like a secret. |
| `private` | `true` for a value that belongs to whoever set it, not to the bot: the address of a server of theirs, an id of an account of theirs, a safety switch. It is saved on their computer (`.circuit/local.json`), not in the shared project, so sharing or syncing a project neither gives it away nor turns a switch on for someone else. The bot gets it like any other setting. Secrets are private anyway. |
| `choices` | For `select`: the values and what the list shows, `{ json = "JSON file", sqlite = "SQLite" }`, in that order. |
| `min`, `max` | For `number` and `slider`: the smallest and largest value. |

Texts, secrets and numbers are boxes with the name above them; switches (`boolean`) and lists (`select`) sit on the right of their name. A page whose required setting has no value shows how many in the list; one with a value that doesn't fit shows that in red, and Save waits until it's fixed. An unchanged default isn't written into the project.

Secrets other than the token reach an exported bot through `.env` as `XC_SECRET_<KEY>` (`XC_SECRET_SPOTIFYCLIENTSECRET`).

### Elements

Besides texts, secrets, choices, switches and numbers, a page can hold these. XC Circuit draws them with its UI kit, the same buttons, fields, sliders and colours its own pages use, so a plugin's page looks and behaves like the rest of the app, in every theme.

| `type` | What it is | Its own keys | The value a bot gets |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `textarea` | Several lines of text | `rows` (2 to 20, default 4) | Text |
| `color` | A colour picker | — | `"#RRGGBB"` |
| `slider` | A slider with the number beside it | `min` (0), `max` (100), `step`, `suffix` (`" XP"`) | A number |
| `list` | A list of texts, with + Add and a remove button on each | `placeholder` for each | A list of texts, `[]` when empty |
| `path` | A file (or, with `pick = "folder"`, a folder) on this computer, with Browse… | `pick` | Text |
| `note` | A box of text, no value | `tone`: `"info"` (default), `"warning"` or `"success"`; `label` is its title (optional) | — |
| `link` | A button that opens a web page, no value | `url` (`https://` only), `button` (default *Open*) | — |

```toml
[settings]
lvlAbout  = { type = "note", page = "levels", description = "Members earn XP for each message." }
lvlXp     = { type = "slider", page = "levels", label = "XP for a level", min = 50, max = 1000, step = 50, default = 100, suffix = " XP" }
lvlColor  = { type = "color", page = "levels", label = "Rank card colour", default = "#00D8F0" }
lvlText   = { type = "textarea", page = "levels", label = "Level-up message", rows = 3, default = "GG ${user}!" }
lvlNoXp   = { type = "list", page = "levels", label = "Channels without XP", placeholder = "Channel id", default = [] }
lvlImage  = { type = "path", page = "levels", label = "Card background" }
lvlDocs   = { type = "link", page = "levels", label = "How levels work", url = "https://example.com/levels", button = "Read" }
```

The DemoBot example has a page like this: `plugins/demo.custom/settings/levels.toml`.

## Plugin settings

Any plugin can add pages and settings to Bot › Settings, without a build mode of its own: list TOML files in [`contributes.botSettings`](./plugin-toml#contributes). A file has the same `[[pages]]` and `[settings]` as a mode, and `modes` to show them only for some build modes:

```toml
# plugins/my.database/settings.toml
modes = ["discord-bot", "fluxer-bot"]   # leave out for every mode

[[pages]]
id = "databases"
name = "Databases"
icon = "database"
description = "Where your bot keeps its data."
order = 25

[settings]
dbKind     = { type = "select", page = "databases", group = "Connection", label = "Kind", choices = { mariadb = "MariaDB / MySQL", postgres = "PostgreSQL" }, default = "mariadb" }
dbHost     = { page = "databases", group = "Connection", label = "Host", placeholder = "localhost" }
dbPort     = { type = "number", page = "databases", group = "Connection", label = "Port", default = 3306, min = 1, max = 65535 }
dbPassword = { type = "secret", page = "databases", group = "Connection", label = "Password" }
dbLog      = { type = "boolean", page = "databases", group = "Debugging", label = "Log every query", default = false }
```

Setting keys are shared by the mode and every plugin: one that's taken already isn't shown, and the Problems panel says so. Start yours with something of your own (`dbHost`, `myPluginKey`). Secrets reach a running bot and an exported one's `.env` like the mode's.

## dependencies

npm packages the runtime libraries need, installed before Run and listed in an export's `package.json`. Blocks add their own with [`requires.dependencies`](./blocks#requires).


---

<!-- docs/api/runtime-libs.md · https://xcrafttm.github.io/XC-Circuit/api/runtime-libs -->

# Runtime libraries

::: info In short
Code a build mode runs when the bot starts: it creates the client, logs in, and gives the blocks a shared API (`ctx.discord`, `ctx.fluxer`).
:::

A runtime library is code a build mode runs when the bot starts: it creates the client (discord.js, fluxer.js), logs in, and gives the mode's blocks a shared API. A mode names its libraries in [`runtimeLibs`](./build-modes#keys).

```js
// plugins/acme.chat/runtime/chat.js
module.exports = {
  id: "chat",                         // blocks get the API as ctx.chat

  setup(rt) {
    const { Client } = rt.require("acme-chat");
    const client = new Client();
    client.on("error", (e) => rt.log.error(`Chat: ${e.message}`));
    return { client, prefix: () => rt.setting("prefix") || "!" };
  },

  async start(rt, api) {
    const token = rt.secret("token");
    if (!token) throw new Error("No bot token set. Add it in Bot › Settings.");
    api.client.once("ready", () => rt.log.success(`Logged in as ${api.client.user.name}`));
    await api.client.login(token);
  },
};
```

## When they run

1. **`setup(rt)`** for each library, in order. What it returns becomes `ctx[id]` for every block.
2. Blocks' own `setup(ctx)`.
3. Event blocks' [`listen(ctx, emit)`](./blocks#listen): they subscribe to the client now, before it connects.
4. **`start(rt, api)`** for each library: connect and log in. A thrown error is shown in the Console.
5. [`ctx.runtime.onStart`](./ctx#runtime) handlers.

## rt

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `rt.require(name)` | Loads an npm package (list it in the mode's [`[dependencies]`](./build-modes#dependencies)). |
| `rt.setting(key)` | A setting of Bot › Settings. |
| `rt.secret(key)` | A secret setting: from the credential store when run from the editor, from `.env` in an exported bot. `rt.secret("token")` is the bot token. |
| `rt.log.info/success/warn/error/debug(...)` | Writes to the Console. |
| `rt.intents()` | The Discord intents the blocks in the project need (their `requires.intents`). |

Look at `plugins/xc.discord/runtime/discord.js` and `plugins/xc.fluxer/runtime/fluxer.js` for complete libraries.


---

<!-- docs/api/pin-types.md · https://xcrafttm.github.io/XC-Circuit/api/pin-types -->

# Pin types

::: info In short
Types of values on wires (`discord.member`, `fluxer.message`…): their name, colour, how to check a value, what they convert to, and how to find one by its id.
:::

Pin types are the types of values that go through wires besides the basic ones (`text`, `number`, `boolean`, `date`, `object`, `list<…>`, `any`). They're TOML files listed in a plugin's `contributes.pinTypes`, each with one `[[type]]` table per type.

```toml
[[type]]
id = "discord.member"
name = "Member"
extends = "object"
color = "#6C7BFF"
icon = "user"
check = "v => v?.constructor?.name === 'GuildMember'"
description = "A person inside one server, with roles and a nickname."

[[type.converts]]
to = "discord.user"
via = "v => v.user"
```

## Keys

| Key | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | **Required.** `plugin.name`, used in [type strings](./fields#type-strings). |
| `name` | Shown on pins and in tooltips. |
| `extends` | The type this one fits into, usually `object`. A `discord.member` pin can connect where an `object` is expected. |
| `color` | The colour of its pins and wires. Themes can change it. |
| `icon` | An icon name. |
| `check` | A JavaScript function (as text) that tells whether a value is of this type. The runtime uses it to recognise values to [convert](#conversions). |
| `description` | What the type is, for tooltips. |
| `fromId` | A JavaScript function (as text), `(id, ctx) => value`, that finds a value of this type by its id. Inputs of this type (or of a type that extends it) can then take an id instead. See [Finding values by id](#finding-values-by-id). |

## Conversions

`[[type.converts]]` lets a value of this type go where another type is needed. `via` is a JavaScript function (as text) that turns the value into the other type when the block runs.

```toml
[[type.converts]]
to = "discord.user"
via = "v => v.user"
```

Now a Member output connects to a User input, and the block gets the member's user. The runtime converts a wired value when it passes this type's `check`, so a type needs `check` for its conversions to work. Lists are converted item by item; inputs of type `any` get the value as it is.

Blocks never give Collections (discord.js's and Fluxer's Maps of things by id): the runtime gives each Collection a block outputs as a list of its items, and a Collection that reaches a `list<…>` input becomes one too. So a block's `list<discord.member>` output can return `guild.members.cache` as it is.

## Finding values by id

With `fromId`, an input of this type can also be given an id: typed into the block or wired in as text. The runtime finds the value before the block runs, so the block always gets the real thing.

```toml
[[type]]
id = "discord.channel"
fromId = "(id, ctx) => ctx.discord.client.channels.fetch(id)"
```

- The function gets the id without spaces or mention marks (`<#123>` becomes `123`) and the block's [`ctx`](./ctx). It can return a promise.
- Types that `extend` it use it too: a `discord.thread` input takes a thread's id.
- In the editor, such inputs start as pins (also when the block says `pin: "only"`) and can be switched to a box for the id, with the pin toggle.
- An empty box gives the block nothing, as an unconnected pin does. An id that finds nothing stops the block with "Channel: no channel with the id …".

The Discord and Fluxer plugins have it on their channel types, so every channel input (categories, threads and voice channels too) takes a channel id.

## Class catalogs

A class catalog tells the editor what members the values behind pin types have, for completion inside `${…}` (`${member.roles.highest.name}`). It's a JSON file listed in `contributes.classes`:

```json
{
  "source": "discord.js 14.28.0",
  "roots": { "discord.user": "User", "discord.member": "GuildMember" },
  "classes": {
    "User": {
      "members": [
        { "name": "username", "kind": "property", "type": "Text" },
        { "name": "avatar", "kind": "property", "type": "Text", "optional": true },
        { "name": "displayAvatarURL", "kind": "method", "type": "Text", "doc": "The avatar's address." }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

| Key | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `source` | What it was made from. |
| `roots` | The class behind each pin type. |
| `classes` | Classes by name, each with `members`. |
| member `name` | The property or method name. |
| member `kind` | `property`, `getter` or `method`. |
| member `type` | How its type is shown: `Text`, `Number`, `Yes/no`, `Date` or a class name. |
| member `optional` | It can be empty. |
| member `class` | The class of its value, when that has members of its own (completion goes on after the next `.`). |
| member `doc` | A short description. |

The Discord plugin makes its catalog from discord.js's type definitions with `node plugins/xc.discord/tools/discordjs-catalog.js`; only methods that read are listed.


---

<!-- docs/api/themes.md · https://xcrafttm.github.io/XC-Circuit/api/themes -->

# Themes

::: info In short
A TOML file with colours (and a few shapes) for the editor. Picked in Settings › Appearance.
:::

A theme sets the editor's colours and a few shapes. Themes are TOML files listed in a plugin's `contributes.themes`, and are picked in Settings › Appearance. The accent colour can also be changed there, on top of any theme.

```toml
id   = "midnight"
name = "Midnight"
base = "dark"

[colors]
frame       = "#0A0D10"
panel       = "#11161B"
canvas      = "#0D1115"
canvasDots  = "#00D8F014"
node        = "#18212A"
text        = "#E4F1F4"
accent      = "#00E5FF"
action      = "#3DFF6E"

[pinColors]
text = "#F5C451"
"discord.member" = "#8A7BFF"

[shape]
nodeRadius = 9
wireWidth  = 2.6

[motion]
speed = 1.0
```

## Keys

| Key | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | **Required.** Unique id. |
| `name` | Shown in Settings. |
| `base` | `"dark"` or `"light"`: the defaults for colours the theme doesn't set. |

## colors

Colours are `#RRGGBB` or `#RRGGBBAA`. Any you leave out come from `base`.

| Key | Used for |
| --- | --- |
| `frame` | the window frame and title bar |
| `panel` | panels and side bars |
| `panelHeader` | panel headers and tab bars |
| `canvas` | the canvas background |
| `canvasDots` | the dot grid on the canvas |
| `node` | block bodies |
| `nodeHeader` | block title bars |
| `nodeBorder` | block outlines |
| `field` | text boxes and fields |
| `line` | separators |
| `text` | text |
| `textMuted` | secondary text |
| `accent` | selection, links, highlights |
| `action` | action wires and the Run button |
| `statusBar` | the status bar |
| `statusText` | text in the status bar |
| `error` | errors |
| `warning` | warnings |

## pinColors

Pin and wire colours by type id: the basic types `text`, `number`, `boolean`, `date`, `any`, `object`, `list`, and any [pin type](./pin-types) such as `discord.member`.

## shape

| Key | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodeRadius` | `9` | Corner radius of blocks. |
| `wireWidth` | `2.6` | Width of wires. |

## motion

| Key | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `speed` | `1.0` | Speed of animations; `0` turns them off. |

Circuit Core's themes (`plugins/xc.core/themes/`) are good starting points.


---

<!-- docs/api/locales.md · https://xcrafttm.github.io/XC-Circuit/api/locales -->

# Translations

::: info In short
A TOML file per language: the app's English texts and their translations.
:::

A translation is a TOML file per language in a plugin, listed in `contributes.locales`. It translates the interface by its English texts. Blocks are not translated. See the [tutorial](/tutorials/translate) for how to start one from the app.

```toml
[meta]
code = "de"
name = "Deutsch"           # the language's own name, shown in the picker
english_name = "German"

[strings]
"Save and close" = "Speichern und schließen"
"{count} to fix" = "{count} zu beheben"
"Run" = ""                 # empty: shown in English
```

## meta

| Key | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `code` | The language code: `de`, `fr`, `pt-BR`. |
| `name` | The language's name in itself. |
| `english_name` | Its name in English. |

## strings

Each key is an English text exactly as the app shows it; each value its translation.

- Keep `{placeholders}` such as `{count}` or `{name}`: the app fills them in. You may move them.
- Empty values fall back to English.
- Several plugins can add to the same language. The app's own texts are in Circuit Core's file; each build mode translates its own category names and settings in its plugin.

Settings › Appearance › *Create a translation…* writes a file with every text of the app to fill in. Files reload when saved.


---

<!-- docs/api/templates.md · https://xcrafttm.github.io/XC-Circuit/api/templates -->

# Templates

::: info In short
Finished bots in a plugin's `templates/` folder, offered under *Start from* in File › New Project.
:::

Templates are the starters File › New Project offers: working bots people begin from. A plugin adds them by putting project folders into its `templates/` folder; they don't need to be listed in `plugin.toml`.

```
acme.chat/
└─ templates/
   └─ basics/
      ├─ template.json
      ├─ circuit.project.json
      └─ workspaces/
         ├─ ping.json
         └─ help.json
```

Each template is an ordinary [project](./project-format) with a `template.json`:

```json
{
  "name": "Basic commands",
  "description": "!ping shows how fast the bot answers, !help lists the commands.",
  "mode": "fluxer-bot"
}
```

| Key | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `name` | Shown in the list of starters. |
| `description` | One or two sentences: what the bot does and what to set up. |
| `mode` | The [build mode](./build-modes) it's for. Default: the `mode` in its `circuit.project.json`. New Project only offers it for that mode. |

Creating a project from a template copies its project file, slash commands and workspaces under a new project id (other files, such as a `plugins/` folder, are not copied), gives it the name typed in New Project, and adds a `.gitignore` for `.circuit/`. The app's own starters are in `examples/templates/`.

Tips:

- Say in the description what has to be filled in (a role id, a channel).
- Keep templates small and readable: people learn from them.


---

<!-- docs/api/project-format.md · https://xcrafttm.github.io/XC-Circuit/api/project-format -->

# Project format

::: info In short
A project is a folder: `circuit.project.json` (name, mode, shared settings), `commands/*.json` (one slash command each), `workspaces/*.json` (one per canvas: blocks, wires, Try Zones, notes) and `.circuit/local.json` (what stays on your computer).
:::

A project is a folder. All files are JSON, written with stable key order and indentation so they diff well in Git.

```
My Bot/
├─ circuit.project.json
├─ commands/
│  └─ <name>.json
├─ workspaces/
│  └─ <key>.json
├─ plugins/          optional: project plugins
└─ .circuit/         this computer's part (leave out of Git)
   ├─ local.json     where the bot is uploaded to, database connections, private settings
   ├─ data/          the bot's stored data
   └─ run/           the folder the bot runs from
```

This is **layout 2**, written since XC Circuit 0.3.0. What is shared (what the bot is) and what is yours alone (where it runs) are kept apart, so a project can be put into Git or synced without your server's address in it.

A project of layout 1 (one `circuit.json` holding everything) is brought to layout 2 when it is opened; its `circuit.json` is kept in `.circuit/layout-1/`. Older versions of XC Circuit can't open a layout 2 project: they look for `circuit.json` and find none.

## circuit.project.json

```json
{
  "layout": 2,
  "id": "8cd7c5b5ae95edcb6b839ba00c48b6ae",
  "name": "DemoBot",
  "mode": "discord-bot",
  "plugins": { "xc.core": "1.0.0", "xc.discord": "1.0.0" },
  "settings": { "prefix": "!" },
  "folders": ["Commands", "Events"]
}
```

| Key | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `layout` | The version of the project folder's layout, `2`. A version of XC Circuit that only knows older layouts doesn't open the project and says which update it needs; a project of an older layout is brought up to date step by step when it opens. |
| `id` | What tells this project from every other, wherever its folder is. Saved secrets and backups go by it. |
| `name` | The bot's name. |
| `mode` | The [build mode](./build-modes) id. |
| `plugins` | Plugins the project uses, with the versions it was saved with. |
| `settings` | Bot › Settings values that are shared: no secrets, and nothing that says where your databases or servers are. Of `databases` only each one's `id`, `name` and `kind`. |
| `data` | Project-wide data: `slashFolders` (the side bar's folders for slash commands, in order) and anything [editor plugins](./editor#changing-the-project) keep. |
| `folders` | Workspace folders in the order of the Workspaces panel. A folder in a folder is its path with `/`, such as `Tickets/Archive`. |
| `order` | Workspace keys in the side bar's order, when it isn't their files' order (by name). |
| `commandOrder` | Slash commands in the side bar's order, when it isn't their files' order. |

## Commands

Each file in `commands/` is one slash command: a list of its entries. A plain command has one; a command with subcommands has one per subcommand (and one per group).

```json
[
  { "name": "ticket open", "description": "Opens a ticket", "options": [] },
  { "name": "ticket close", "description": "Closes it", "options": [] }
]
```

An entry's `folder` and `disabled` are its side bar folder and whether it's turned off. The file is named after the command (`ticket.json`).

## .circuit/local.json

What belongs to this computer, not to the bot:

```json
{
  "hosting": { "kind": "sftp", "host": "203.0.113.7", "user": "bot", "folder": "/home/bot" },
  "settings": { "devServer": "123456789012345678" },
  "databases": { "main": { "host": "db.example", "port": 5432, "user": "bot" } }
}
```

| Key | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `hosting` | Where Bot › Remote… uploads the bot (`kind`, `host`, `port`, `user`, `folder`, `panel`, `server` …; no passwords or keys). |
| `settings` | Private settings, by key. |
| `databases` | Where each database is, by its id: everything of a connection but its `id`, `name` and `kind`. |
| `more` | The blocks whose More options are open, by workspace: their `uid`s. |

In the editor, to plugins and in the running bot the project is whole: `settings` and `data` hold the shared and the local parts together, as before.

## Workspaces

Each file in `workspaces/` is one workspace; its file name without `.json` is its **key**.

```json
{
  "name": "Startup",
  "folder": "Events",
  "nodes": {
    "1": { "block": "core.on_start@1", "at": [40, 60] },
    "2": {
      "block": "core.increase_stored@1",
      "at": [340, 60],
      "values": { "scope": "global", "key": "starts", "by": 1 }
    },
    "3": {
      "block": "core.log@1",
      "at": [660, 60],
      "values": { "message": "Started ${value} times", "level": "success" }
    }
  },
  "links": ["1.next > 2.in", "2.next > 3.in", "2.value > 3.value"]
}
```

| Key | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `name` | Shown in the Workspaces panel. |
| `folder` | The folder it's listed in (a path such as `Tickets/Archive` for a folder in a folder). |
| `nodes` | Blocks by id (the number shown in their title bar). |
| `links` | Wires. |
| `zones` | Try Zones by id. |
| `notes` | Notes on the canvas, by id. [Below](#notes). |
| `disabled` | `true`: the workspace is turned off and left out when the bot runs or is exported. Missing: it is on. |

### Nodes

| Key | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `block` | The block id and its major version: `discord.send_message@3`. |
| `uid` | What tells this block from every other for good. Its number (the key it is kept under) is easy to read, but two people who each add a block get the same next number; `uid` is what their work can be put together by. XC Circuit writes it; a block without one gets one. |
| `at` | Position on the canvas `[x, y]`. |
| `values` | Field values by key. Missing fields have their default. |
| `pins` | Fields switched to pins. |
| `zone` | The Try Zone the block is in. |
| `heights` | Heights of resized text boxes, by field. |
| `width` | The block's width, when resized. |

### Links

A link is `"from > to"`, each side `node.pin`:

- `"1.next > 2.in"`: an action wire from block 1's `next` output (or one of its `flows`) to block 2's action input `in`.
- `"2.value > 3.value"`: a value wire from block 2's output `value` to block 3's input `value` (a field or a `${…}` name).
- A Try Zone's outputs are wired from the zone id: `"z1.done > 5.in"`, `"z1.error > 6.in"`, `"z1.message > 6.message"`.

### Zones

```json
"zones": { "z1": { "title": "Reply", "rect": [740, 40, 380, 260], "retry": 2, "timeoutMs": 5000 } }
```

| Key | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `title` | Shown on the zone. |
| `rect` | `[x, y, width, height]`, worked out from its blocks. |
| `retry` | How many times to try again. |
| `timeoutMs` | Give up after this many milliseconds. |

### Notes

```json
"notes": { "n1": { "title": "Rank reply", "text": "Builds the embed and replies.", "rect": [0, -80, 1100, 620], "color": "#F5C451" } }
```

| Key | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `title` | Shown in the note's title band. |
| `text` | The description, under the title. |
| `rect` | `[x, y, width, height]` on the canvas. |
| `color` | `#RRGGBB`; missing: the theme's accent. |
| `loose` | `true`: dragging the note leaves the blocks inside where they are (new notes have this). Missing: they move with it. |

Notes don't run: they only explain and group blocks in the editor.
